title: Adaptive Retrieval Strategies for Low-Resource Question Answering
problem_statement: Current retrieval-augmented QA systems degrade sharply when the target language or domain has little indexed text, yet most retrieval-strategy research assumes high-resource corpora. This gap leaves practitioners in low-resource settings without a principled way to choose or adapt a retrieval strategy.
literature_gap: Prior work (Lewis et al. 2020; Karpukhin et al. 2020) evaluates dense retrieval almost exclusively on high-resource English benchmarks. Low-resource retrieval studies (e.g. Zhang et al. 2022) focus on translation-based pipelines rather than adaptive strategy selection, leaving open how a system should decide between sparse, dense, and hybrid retrieval as available indexed text shrinks.
research_questions: How does retrieval strategy performance (sparse vs. dense vs. hybrid) degrade as indexed corpus size decreases across five typologically distinct languages?
Can a lightweight corpus-size signal be used to automatically select an appropriate retrieval strategy at query time?
methodology: A controlled corpus-subsampling study across five languages, comparing BM25, a dense bi-encoder, and a hybrid reranker at six corpus-size tiers, followed by training a lightweight strategy-selection classifier on the resulting performance curves and validating it on two held-out languages.

timeline.milestone: Literature review and corpus preparation complete
